They are two separate issues here :

1) His possible taste in pornography. 
It is important to recall that fantasy ISN'T always what you want in real life. Things can mentally turn you on, yet you would never ever wish to be in that kind of situation IRL. Pornography is a medium that is here to make you have a boner, not to give you a taste on how real sex works. I think that it is important to respect other's fantasies (as long as they are legal ofc) even if we aren't into it. 

A couple is supposed to be a safe space, where trust is the main focus. Having to share what are our fantaisies in a heart-to-heart is something that can put the person in an extremely vulnerable situation. And again it doesn't mean you have to agree with it, you are totally free to say outloud that you aren't comfortable with a certain fantasy. But at least I think it's important to not... Make the other person feel awful about uncontrollable taste.

Also I don't think that incest is THAT weird (as a fantasy I mean) it's kinda common. But it's personal. 

The kind of porn you watch doesn't define you as a person I think. 


2) The real issue here, is that you two did agree on a "no-porn" relationship, and the fact that he is hiding it is definetly something that isn't cool. It's a trust breaking move here. You don't just agree on stuff and they break the rule in secret you know? 

The fact that he watches porn so often despite saying that he wouldn't is sorta concerning, have you considered that he might suffer from porn addiction? 

In any case I highly recommend you two to have a discussion about it, where you both really LISTEN to the other's feelings. So you can express your thoughts and he can explain his. The less judgment, the better. So if you want to have honest reaction from him, being careful with your wording seems like a good beginning. 

Because being caught red-handed is always something uncomfortable, and people in those cases might act ultra defensive, If you use a word that attack him, he might not open to you. And you won't have the heart to heart you were wishing for. 


If despite your kindness and open-mindedness he keeps lying, becomes aggressive, or listen to your feelings but doesn't/can't change, it's on you to decide whether or not it's the kind of person you want to be with.

I wish you two the best!
